name: Hack Squat
description: The hack squat is a machine-based squat variation where the lifter stands on an angled platform and pushes a sled upward. The fixed back-pad support eliminates lower back involvement, allowing very heavy quadriceps loading. Foot position can be varied to emphasize different portions of the quads.

execution.starting_position: Stand on the platform with feet shoulder-width apart and the back and shoulders against the pads. Unhook the safety handles. Feet can be placed lower for more quad emphasis.
execution.setup_instructions: Load the machine with appropriate weight. Set the sled to a starting position you can safely unrack. Keep the back flat against the pad throughout.
steps: Release the safety handles and lower the sled by bending the knees.
Descend until knees reach approximately 90 degrees or deeper.
Press through the whole foot to extend the knees and push the sled back to the top position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the platform — place feet high enough on the platform
Locking the knees out aggressively at the top
safety_considerations: Always use the safety catches — do not unrack without them engaged first
Re-engage safety catches before stepping off the machine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: 90-degree knee flexion at the bottom. Full extension (no hyperextension) at the top.
coaching_cues: Press through the whole foot — do not rise onto the toes
Keep the back welded to the pad throughout the entire set
